mainTopic: Which offerings need נסכים: one animal for a vowed עולה, the תודה, the 'not already obligated' rule, separate נסכים for every animal, and the מצורע's offerings.
overview: This amud continues the ברייתא about נסכים (the flour, oil and wine that come with certain offerings) and the words of the פסוקים in במדבר 15. First, the גמרא explains how רבי יונתן and רבי יאשיה each know that a person who vowed an עולה may bring just one animal, either cattle or sheep. Next, it explains why a תודה needs its own source for נסכים: we might have thought its four kinds of bread take their place. Then it shows that the word 'עולה' narrows a כלל ופרט וכלל. The result is that a קרבן needs נסכים only if the person was not already obligated to bring it, so cases like ולדות קדשים and תמורה are included, while בכור, מעשר and פסח are not. After that, the גמרא goes through each extra 'או' in the passage, and each one teaches that two offerings brought together never share one set of נסכים, in any combination. Finally, it begins the source for the משנה's rule that a מצורע's חטאת and אשם need נסכים, and raises a challenge that is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: The extra 'and' makes it sound like both animals are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רבי יונתן needs a special פסוק: the 'and' in 'and of the flock' makes it sound as if the word 'together' were written.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is written 'and of the flock,' it is as if 'together' were written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from the previous daf. Why does רבי יונתן need the word 'או' (or) to teach that one animal is enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן normally holds that two items listed in a פסוק count separately, unless the word יחדו (together) appears. Here, though, ויקרא 1:2 says 'מן הבקר ומן הצאן' with a connecting 'and.' That makes it sound like both animals are required, as if יחדו were written. So the 'או' in במדבר 15:3 is needed to teach that one animal is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because
Together. This word in a פסוק shows that two listed items must go together.
It is as if it were written

phrases.english: Since it is written: 'And of the flock,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:2. The point is the little 'and' that connects the flock to the herd.

phrases.english: it is as though 'together' were written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous daf about why רבי יונתן needs the פסוק 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual reading: the connecting 'and' works like the word יחדו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי יונתן, items listed in a פסוק are automatically separate, so no extra פסוק should be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'and' in ויקרא 1:2 makes it sound like both animals are required, so the 'או' is needed to undo that impression.

steps.title: How does רבי יאשיה know one animal is enough?
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יאשיה, items listed together are always treated as a pair. So he should need a פסוק to teach that one animal is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי יאשיה, who says that even without 'together' written it is as if 'together' were written, a פסוק should be needed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the other opinion, רבי יאשיה, and raises a difficulty: where does he learn that one animal is enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה holds that any two items listed in a פסוק must go together, even without the word יחדו. By his rule, 'מן הבקר ומן הצאן' should require both animals. So he needs some source that teaches that one animal is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
A פסוק should be needed; there should be a source for this

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yoshiya, who said:
even though 'together' is not written,
it is as though 'together' were written,
a verse should be required!
phrases.notes: He means: by רבי יאשיה's rule both animals would be needed, so where does he learn that one is enough?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי יונתן, the גמרא checks how the other opinion handles the same law.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יאשיה's view that items listed together are always a pair
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If listed items always go together, then 'מן הבקר ומן הצאן' requires both animals. Some source must be needed to allow just one.

steps.title: Two separate פסוקים show that one animal is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה learns it from ויקרא chapter 1, where the עולה from cattle and the עולה from sheep appear in two separate פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it written: 'If his offering is an עולה from the herd,' and separately, 'And if his offering is from the flock'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on רבי יאשיה. The תורה itself lists the cattle עולה and the sheep עולה in two separate פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה's rule applies only when two items appear together in one phrase. Here the תורה gives each animal its own פסוק, starting with 'if.' That clearly shows each animal is a complete option by itself, so even רבי יאשיה agrees that one animal is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned entirely on the מזבח
Cattle; the herd
Sheep or goats; the flock

phrases.english: Isn't it written: 'If his offering is a burnt offering of the herd,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:3

phrases.english: 'And if his offering is of the flock'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:10. This is a separate פסוק, and that separation is the whole proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכְתִיב: אִם עֹלָה קׇרְבָּנוֹ מִן הַבָּקָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different source: the separate פסוקים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יאשיה would have no source allowing just one animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two separate 'if' פסוקים show that each animal is a full option by itself.

steps.title: Why רבי יונתן still needs the extra פסוק: an unspecified vow
steps.stepSummary: Why doesn't רבי יונתן learn from the separate פסוקים too? Because without 'או' we might think they only cover someone who named one animal. Someone who vowed without saying which animal might have to bring both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other? It was needed. You might have thought: that applies only when he specified. But if he vowed without specifying, let him bring from both. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יונתן needs the 'או' at all, since the separate פסוקים already exist. It answers that the 'או' teaches something new about a vow made without saying which animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The separate פסוקים might only cover a person who said 'I will bring a cow' or 'I will bring a sheep.' If someone just said 'I take upon myself an עולה' without saying which, we might think he must bring both to be safe. The 'או' in במדבר 15:3 teaches that even then, one animal is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one; the other opinion
It was necessary
It would have entered your mind to say; you might have thought
He specified clearly
Without specifying; an unclear or general vow
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that one animal is enough for an עולה. רבי יאשיה learns it from the separate פסוקים in ויקרא 1. רבי יונתן learns it from 'או' in במדבר 15:3, which covers even a vow made without specifying the animal.
steps.confusionAlert: 'ואידך' here means רבי יונתן, the opinion from step 1, not רבי יאשיה. The question is why he doesn't just use the separate פסוקים like רבי יאשיה does.

phrases.english: And the other? It was necessary:
phrases.notes: 'The other' is רבי יונתן. The question is left unsaid: why does he need the 'או' if the separate פסוקים already exist?

phrases.english: it would enter your mind to say:

phrases.english: but without specification,

It teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יונתן and asks why the separate פסוקים from step 3 aren't enough for him.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: a specified vow versus an unspecified vow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The separate פסוקים might only allow one animal when the person named which animal. An unspecified vow might require both.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'או' teaches that even an unspecified vow is fulfilled with one animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law: a person who says 'הרי עלי עולה' without details fulfills his vow with just one animal, either cattle or sheep.

steps.title: The ברייתא learns the תודה from the words 'or a sacrifice'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא: the source that a תודה needs נסכים is the phrase 'או זבח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: From where do we know that a thanks offering needs libations? The verse says: 'Or a sacrifice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא so it can examine it. This line is setting up the question that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already learned שלמים from the word 'זבח'. Now it says the extra word 'או' ('or') brings in the תודה. This makes it sound as if the תודה would not be covered by the word 'זבח' alone.

keyTerms.meaning: A thanks offering, a type of שלמים that is brought together with loaves of bread
Libations: the flour, oil and wine brought along with certain offerings
'The verse says', used to bring a source from a פסוק
A sacrifice, here meaning a שלמים-type offering

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: He is quoting the ברייתא the גמרא has been working through.

phrases.english: From where do we know a thanks offering [needs libations]?
The verse says: 'Or a sacrifice.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:3. The extra word 'or' is what brings in the תודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of one animal or both, to the next line of the ברייתא about the תודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תודה needs נסכים, learned from the word 'או' in 'או זבח'.

steps.title: Isn't a thanks offering already a sacrifice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a special word is needed for the תודה, since it is plainly a זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that a thanks offering is not a sacrifice?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. A תודה is obviously a זבח, so the word 'זבח' should already include it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'זבח' covers all שלמים, and a תודה is a kind of שלמים, then using 'או' to include it seems pointless. The גמרא wants to know why the תודה needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say...?' A question that pushes back on something that seems obvious

phrases.english: Is that to say a thanks offering is not a sacrifice?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 5 as unneeded.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'או' to include the תודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תודה is already a זבח, so the word 'זבח' should cover it without any extra word.

steps.title: We might have thought the bread replaces the libations
steps.stepSummary: The extra word is needed, because we might have thought that a תודה, which comes with bread, does not also need נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since bread comes along with it, it should not need libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תודה needed its own source. Without it, we might have thought the bread takes the place of the נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה is a זבח, but it is unusual because loaves come with it. We could have thought those loaves fill the job of the נסכים, so the פסוק had to tell us that it still needs them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was needed': the extra source is not wasted
'You might have thought': brings in a mistaken idea the פסוק comes to block
Bread, here the loaves that come with the תודה

phrases.english: It was needed,
since you might have thought:
since there is bread with it,
it should not need libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by showing a real reason the תודה needs its own source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that the extra word is needed to block a possible mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a תודה comes with bread, the bread might take the place of the נסכים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'או' teaches that the תודה still needs נסכים.

steps.title: The נזיר's ram also comes with bread and still needs libations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the איל נזיר also comes with bread and needs נסכים, so why would we ever have thought differently about the תודה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is it different from the nazirite's ram, which has bread with it and still needs libations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 7. We already know from the איל נזיר that bread does not cancel the need for נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says clearly that the נזיר's ram comes with bread and with נסכים. So the mistaken idea from step 7 should never have come up, and the extra word for the תודה seems unneeded again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And how is it different?' A challenge comparing two cases that seem the same
The ram a נזיר brings at the end of his נזירות, which comes with bread and נסכים

phrases.english: And how is it different from the nazirite's ram,
which has bread with it,
and still needs libations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'you might have thought' of step 7 using the איל נזיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that bread might replace נסכים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The איל נזיר has bread and still needs נסכים, so we would already know the same for the תודה.

steps.title: Two kinds of bread versus four kinds
steps.stepSummary: The נזיר brings only two kinds of bread, while the תודה brings four, so we might have thought the תודה is different. The פסוק teaches that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: there, it is two kinds; here, it is four kinds. So the verse teaches us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are not the same. The large amount of bread with the תודה might have made us think it does not need נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איל נזיר only shows that two kinds of bread do not replace נסכים. The תודה has four kinds, so we could have thought that much bread is enough to replace them. That is why the תודה needed its own extra word.

keyTerms.meaning: Two kinds of bread (with the איל נזיר)
Four kinds of bread (with the תודה)
'It teaches us': the source tells us the real הלכה against the mistaken idea

steps.whatToRemember: The תודה needs נסכים even though it comes with four kinds of bread. That is why the ברייתא includes it with its own extra word, 'או'.

phrases.english: You might have thought:
there, [there are] two kinds,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the נזיר's ram, which comes with loaves and wafers.

phrases.english: here, [there are] four kinds,
phrases.notes: The תודה comes with four kinds of bread (ויקרא 7:12–13).

phrases.english: so it teaches us [that it still needs libations].

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הָתָם שְׁנֵי מִינִין, הָכָא אַרְבַּעַת מִינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by pointing out how the תודה differs from the איל נזיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a difference between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Four kinds of bread might be enough to replace נסכים, even though two kinds are not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with four kinds of bread, the תודה still needs נסכים.

steps.title: Why does the verse need the word 'burnt offering'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next part of the פסוק and asks: why write 'עולה' at all, if 'לפלא נדר או לנדבה' would already cover it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the Merciful One just write 'in fulfillment of a vow or as a gift,' and it would not need to say 'burnt offering'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to another part of the ברייתא's פסוק. It challenges the word 'עולה' as extra, because 'a vow or a gift' would already include an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה can be brought as a נדר or a נדבה. So if the פסוק had only said 'to fulfill a vow or as a gift', we would already know an עולה needs נסכים. The word 'עולה' seems extra, and the גמרא is setting up its explanation of what that word adds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let the Merciful One write...': a challenge that a word in the תורה seems extra
A vow, where a person takes on himself to bring an offering
A gift offering, where a person sets aside a specific animal
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write
'In fulfillment of a vow or as a gift,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:3

phrases.english: and it would not need [to say] 'burnt offering'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תודה discussion and starts a new question on another word in the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עולה is already covered by 'a vow or a gift', so writing 'עולה' seems extra.

steps.title: Without the word עולה, the פסוק would be read as a general-detail-general
steps.stepSummary: If עולה were not written, we would read the פסוק as a כלל ופרט וכלל and include every קרבן that does not come for a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had not written 'burnt offering,' I would have said: 'And you will make a fire offering to ה׳' is a general statement. 'In fulfillment of a vow or as a gift' is a detail. 'For a pleasing aroma' goes back to being general. A general, a detail and a general means we include only things similar to the detail. Just as the detail is something that does not come for a sin, so too anything that does not come for a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question from Step 10 by showing how we would have read the פסוק if the word עולה were missing. This sets up the next step, where we see what that reading would wrongly include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has a wide phrase, then a narrow phrase, then a wide phrase again. With that pattern, we include only things that resemble the narrow middle phrase. נדר and נדבה are not brought because of a sin, so the shared feature would be 'does not come for a sin.'

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One: a name for ה׳ as the One who wrote the תורה
I would have thought: an idea we would have had, which the תורה then corrects
A general, wide statement in a פסוק
A detail, a specific narrow statement in a פסוק
General, then detail, then general: a rule of learning that includes only things similar to the detail
Similar to the detail

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the הוה אמינא, what we would have thought. The final reading comes in the next steps, once the word עולה is taken into account.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every קרבן that does not come for a sin would need נסכים

steps.title: That reading would include בכור, מעשר and פסח, so the Torah wrote עולה
steps.stepSummary: Without עולה we would exclude חטאת and אשם but include בכור, מעשר and פסח. The word עולה prevents this.
steps.simpleTranslation: I would exclude a sin offering and a guilt offering, since they come for a sin. I would include a firstborn, an animal tithe and a פסח, since they do not come for a sin. That is why the פסוק says 'burnt offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer: the mistaken reading would make בכור, מעשר and פסח need נסכים. Writing the word עולה stops that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'not for a sin' test, בכור, מעשר and פסח would wrongly be included. The word עולה adds another detail that narrows the group further. It leaves out קרבנות that a person was obligated to bring anyway, as the next steps explain.

steps.title: With עולה written, what does the general-detail-general still include?
steps.stepSummary: Now that עולה narrows things, the גמרא asks what the כלל ופרט וכלל still adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that 'burnt offering' is written, what do you include through the general and the detail?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question: since עולה narrows the group so much, what is left for the כלל ופרט וכלל to include?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלל ופרט וכלל is supposed to add some cases beyond the detail itself. If עולה shrinks the group, the גמרא wants to know which cases are still added. This sets up the answer in the next step.

steps.title: The new test: a קרבן one was not already obligated to bring
steps.stepSummary: The shared feature becomes 'not already obligated': anything like that needs נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the detail is clearly something one was not already obligated to bring, so too anything one was not already obligated to bring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a new test. A קרבן needs נסכים if the person was not already obligated to bring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה brought for a נדר or נדבה becomes required only once the person chooses to take it on. בכור, מעשר and פסח are obligations that exist on their own, so they fail this test. The test is no longer 'not for a sin' but 'not already obligated.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כלל ופרט וכלל includes any קרבן that is not מחוייב ועומד

steps.title: What this includes: offspring, substitutes, and an עולה from leftover funds
steps.stepSummary: The new test includes ולדות קדשים, תמורה, and an עולה bought from מותרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This includes offspring of consecrated animals, their substitutes, and a burnt offering that comes from leftover funds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the actual cases that the כלל ופרט וכלל includes under the new test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these were a set obligation from the start. They came about through a later event: an animal gave birth, someone made a substitute, or money was left over. So, like an עולה of נדר, they need נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring born to consecrated animals
A substitute animal: a regular animal someone tried to swap for a holy one, which becomes holy too
Leftover funds set aside for קרבנות that were not used

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק includes for נסכים any קרבן one was not already obligated to bring (ולדות, תמורה, an עולה from מותרות). It leaves out בכור, מעשר and פסח, and also חטאת and אשם.

phrases.english: This includes offspring of consecrated animals,
and their substitutes,
and a burnt offering that comes from leftover funds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies Step 14's test to specific cases
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ולדות קדשים, תמורה and an עולה from מותרות all require נסכים

steps.title: Two more cases that need נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The list of things included by the 'not already obligated' test goes on. It adds an אשם שניתק לרעיה and all זבחים slaughtered שלא לשמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The test also includes an אשם that was sent off to graze, and every קרבן that was slaughtered not for its own purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the list from step 15 of cases that need נסכים under the new test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם that was sent off to graze no longer serves its original job. If it is brought as an עולה, it is not paying off any obligation. A קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמן does not fulfill the owner's obligation either. Both fit the shared feature of 'not already obligated', so both need נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: An אשם that can no longer be offered for its original purpose. It is sent to graze until it gets a blemish.
Slaughtered with the wrong purpose in mind, not for the purpose it was set aside for.
Animal offerings

steps.whatToRemember: The final list from the כלל ופרט וכלל: ולדות קדשים, תמורה, an עולה from מותרות, an אשם שניתק לרעיה, and זבחים שלא לשמן. None of them pays off an existing obligation, so all of them need נסכים.

phrases.english: and a guilt offering that was sent off to graze,
and all the offerings
that were slaughtered not for their own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of included cases begun in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any קרבן that does not pay off an existing obligation needs נסכים. This includes an אשם שניתק לרעיה and זבחים שלא לשמן.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'a vow OR a gift'?
steps.stepSummary: Earlier, the word או was used for a דרשה. So the גמרא asks why we need the או between נדר and נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said 'or' is there to teach something, why do I need 'to fulfill a vow or as a gift'? Just to separate them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new question about the same פסוק. Since one או teaches a lesson, what does the next או teach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא used an earlier או to teach a דרשה. That means each או should carry meaning. The או between נדר and נדבה looks like it only separates the two words, which seems obvious. The גמרא wants to know what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: For a דרשה, to teach a lesson
To fulfill a vow (a נדר, where a person promises a קרבן)
A gift offering, where a person sets aside a specific animal
To separate them, so each one counts by itself

phrases.english: And now that you said 'or' is for a derivation,
phrases.notes: This refers to the earlier או in 'עולה או זבח', which the גמרא used to teach a lesson.

phrases.english: 'to fulfill a vow or as a gift,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:3

phrases.english: why do I need it? To separate them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כלל ופרט וכלל to the other או words in the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the או between נדר and נדבה teaches.

steps.title: Each one needs נסכים even alone
steps.stepSummary: Without או, we might think you need both a נדר and a נדבה before נסכים are required. The או teaches that each one alone needs נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought that until a person brings both a vow and a gift, no libations are needed. So it teaches that a vow alone needs libations, and a gift alone needs libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the או makes each kind of offering count by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק said 'a vow and a gift', we could read it as one combined case: נסכים only when both are brought. The או splits them. So a נדר alone needs נסכים, and a נדבה alone needs נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
You might have thought (this is the הוה אמינא)
So it teaches us
By itself, alone

phrases.english: It was needed; it would enter your mind to say:
until he brings a vow and a gift,
they should not need libations,
so it teaches us
that if he brought a vow alone, it needs libations,
and if he brought a gift alone,
he must bring libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows the word is needed to block a wrong reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נסכים are needed only when a נדר and a נדבה are brought together.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נדר alone or a נדבה alone each needs נסכים.

steps.title: That fits רבי יאשיה, but what about רבי יונתן?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for רבי יאשיה. But רבי יונתן already reads two items as 'either one', even without או. So why does he need it?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for רבי יאשיה. But for רבי יונתן, why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It only works for one תנא's way of reading פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה holds that two items listed together mean 'both together' unless the פסוק separates them. So for him, the או is needed. רבי יונתן holds that two items mean 'each one alone' even without a separating word. For him, the או seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one opinion)
But (introduces the opinion where it does not work)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. רבי יאשיה needs a word like או to split items. רבי יונתן splits them on his own, so for him או must teach something else.

phrases.english: This works for רבי יאשיה,
phrases.notes: He holds that two things mentioned together count only as a pair, unless the פסוק splits them.

phrases.english: but according to רבי יונתן, why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that או teaches each offering alone needs נסכים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי יונתן, each item already counts alone without או, so this או would add nothing.

steps.title: For רבי יונתן: both together need two sets of נסכים
steps.stepSummary: Even for רבי יונתן, the או is needed. Without it, we might think that someone bringing a נדר and a נדבה together needs only one set of נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: a vow alone needs libations, and a gift alone needs libations, but if he brings both a vow and a gift together, the libations of one are enough. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new job to the או so that it is not wasted for רבי יונתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן already knows that each one alone needs נסכים. The new worry is a case where both are brought together. Maybe one set of נסכים would cover both. The או teaches that each קרבן needs its own נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: It would be enough
Of one

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
if he brought a vow alone, it needs libations;
if he brought a gift alone, it needs libations;
but if he brought a vow and a gift together,
the libations of one would be enough;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: אַיְיתִי נֶדֶר לְחוֹדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a new lesson for רבי יונתן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: When a נדר and a נדבה are brought together, one set of נסכים covers both.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each קרבן needs its own נסכים, even when brought together with another.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a practical rule: bringing two קרבנות at once does not let you share the נסכים.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'or on your festivals'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks what the next או, in או במועדיכם, comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need 'or on your festivals'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues down the פסוק. It asks the same question about the next או.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each או has been given its own lesson so far. So the או before במועדיכם also needs a job. The גמרא is looking for a case that the earlier lessons did not yet cover.

keyTerms.meaning: On your festivals (the רגלים)

phrases.english: Why do I need 'or on your festivals'?
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, במדבר 15:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question about the next או in the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the או before במועדיכם adds.

steps.title: A possible mistake: maybe the rule is only for very different offerings
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins by stating a wrong idea the או comes to block. Maybe 'each needs its own נסכים' applies only when the two offerings differ in both type and kind of promise.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: this rule applies only when he brings an עולה as a vow and a שלמים as a gift, or the other way around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer by describing the wrong idea (the הוה אמינא). The rest of the answer continues after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 taught that two קרבנות brought together each need their own נסכים. Now we might limit that rule to cases where they are different in every way. One example is an עולה from a נדר and a שלמים from a נדבה. The או במועדיכם will come to widen the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only when...
Or also
The opposite, the other way around

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
this applies only where he brings
a burnt offering as a vow and a peace offering as a gift,
or the other way around.
phrases.notes: The other way around means a שלמים as a vow and an עולה as a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 21 by stating the הוה אמינא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: names a wrong reading the word comes to block
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separate נסכים are needed only when the two offerings differ in both type and kind of promise.

steps.title: Completing the answer: same kind of promise still needs separate נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the answer from step 22. Someone might think that a עולה and a שלמים brought under the same kind of promise share one set of נסכים. The או in או במועדיכם teaches that each one needs its own נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where someone brings a עולה and a שלמים both as a נדר, or both as a נדבה, you might say: they share one 'name' of נדר, or one 'name' of נדבה, so נסכים for one should be enough. 'או במועדיכם' teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the wrong idea it started in step 22 and then shows that או במועדיכם blocks that wrong idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said: maybe separate נסכים are needed only when two offerings differ in both type and kind of promise. Here is the other side of that thought. If they differ only in type (עולה and שלמים) but share the same kind of promise, maybe one set of נסכים covers both. The או teaches that even a difference in type alone is enough to require נסכים for each offering.

keyTerms.meaning: One 'name' (category) of נדר: both offerings come from the same kind of promise
It should be enough for him
The נסכים (flour, oil, wine) of just one offering
It teaches us (that the wrong idea is not true)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the pattern for the rest of the section: each או knocks out one more way we might have thought two offerings could share נסכים.

phrases.english: But where one brings
a burnt offering and a peace offering as a vow,
or else a burnt offering and a peace offering as a gift offering,
it is a single name of 'vow'
phrases.notes: He means both offerings fall under the same kind of promise, so they look like one unit.

phrases.english: and it is a single name of 'gift offering',
so it should be enough for him to bring the libations of one;
therefore 'or on your festivals' teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:3.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 22 by stating the opposite case and the lesson of the או.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each extra או rules out one more case where we might have thought נסכים could be shared.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A עולה and a שלמים brought under the same kind of promise might share one set of נסכים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if they share the kind of promise, each offering needs its own נסכים.

steps.title: Why the או in 'עולה או זבח'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next או in the פסוק and asks what 'בן בקר עולה או זבח' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the 'or' in 'And when you make a young bull a עולה or a זבח'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next question: what extra lesson does the או in 'עולה או זבח' teach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier או words already taught several cases. So this או seems extra, and the גמרא wants to find a new case that it covers.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (What does this word add?)
A sacrifice; here it means a שלמים
A young bull

phrases.aramaic: ״וְכִי תַעֲשֶׂה בֶן בָּקָר עֹלָה אוֹ זָבַח״,
phrases.english: 'And when you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:8.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְכִי תַעֲשֶׂה בֶן בָּקָר עֹלָה אוֹ זָבַח״, לְמָה לִי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining או במועדיכם, the גמרא moves to the next או in the passage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new case the או in 'עולה או זבח' teaches.

steps.title: The wrong idea: maybe only different types need separate נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the או was needed and begins describing the mistake we might have made. Maybe the rule of separate נסכים applies only to two different types of offerings, like a עולה and a שלמים under the same promise.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: this rule applies only when someone brings a עולה and a שלמים both as a נדר, or both as a נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by stating a wrong idea. This sets up the next step, where it shows the case this או comes to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 established that two different types of offerings under the same promise each need נסכים. Now the גמרא imagines someone limiting the rule to that case alone, where the type is different. The next step shows the case that would be left out.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
It might enter your mind to say (a wrong first thought)
This rule applies only (in this case)

phrases.english: It was necessary, for it might enter your mind to say:
this applies only where one brings
a burnt offering and a peace offering as a vow,
or else a burnt offering and a peace offering as a gift offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 24 by stating a possible wrong limit on the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting up a הוה אמינא that the או will reject.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule of separate נסכים covers only offerings of different types.

steps.title: Same type, different promise: each still needs נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the answer. Two עולות, or two שלמים, one a נדר and one a נדבה, might seem to share one set of נסכים because they are the same type. The או teaches that each needs its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where someone brings two עולות, one as a נדר and one as a נדבה, or two שלמים, one as a נדר and one as a נדבה, I would say: they share one 'name' of שלמים, or one 'name' of עולה, so נסכים for one should be enough. The או teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the case the או in 'עולה או זבח' comes to cover: same type of offering, but different kinds of promise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 dealt with a different type under the same promise. This step flips it: the same type under a different promise. The או teaches that a difference in the kind of promise alone is also enough to require separate נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: Two burnt offerings
Two peace offerings
I would say
One 'name' (category) of עולה: the same type of offering

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In step 23 the offerings differ in type but share the kind of promise. Here they share the type but differ in the kind of promise.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי שְׁתֵּי עוֹלוֹת,
phrases.english: But where one brings two burnt offerings,
one as a vow and one as a gift offering,
or else two peace offerings,
one as a vow and one as a gift offering,
I would say it is a single name of 'peace offering',
it is a single name of 'burnt offering',
so it should be enough for him to bring the libations of one;
therefore the verse teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי שְׁתֵּי עוֹלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from step 25 by giving the case that the או comes to include.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The או extends the rule to a new case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two offerings of the same type, one a נדר and one a נדבה, might share one set of נסכים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even two offerings of the same type, if they come from different kinds of promise, each need their own נסכים.

steps.title: Why the או in 'לפלא נדר או שלמים'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to yet another או and asks what 'לפלא נדר או שלמים' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the 'or' in 'to fulfill a vow or a שלמים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next question: what does the או in 'לפלא נדר או שלמים' add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: By now the גמרא has covered offerings that differ in type, in kind of promise, or in both. So this או looks extra, and the גמרא looks for a further case it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: To fulfill (literally: to set apart clearly) a vow
Peace offerings

phrases.english: 'In fulfillment of a vow clearly uttered or for peace offerings,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:8, the second half of the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the או in 'עולה או זבח', the גמרא asks about the next או in the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new case the או in 'לפלא נדר או שלמים' teaches.

steps.title: The wrong idea: maybe the rule needs a difference in type or promise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with a wrong idea. Maybe separate נסכים are needed only when the two offerings differ in something, like two עולות or two שלמים where one is a נדר and one is a נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: this rule applies only when someone brings two עולות, one as a נדר and one as a נדבה, or two שלמים, one as a נדר and one as a נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by stating a wrong idea. This only sets up the point. The next step gives the case this או comes to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case from step 26 (same type, different promise) is now treated as the limit someone might put on the rule. The גמרא is preparing to show a case that limit would leave out, which this או then comes to include.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow: 'I take upon myself to bring an offering,' so he must replace it if it is lost
A gift offering: 'This animal is an offering,' tied to that one animal
One

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּמַיְיתֵי שְׁתֵּי עוֹלוֹת,
phrases.english: this applies only where one brings two burnt offerings,
one as a vow and one as a gift offering,
or else two peace offerings,
one as a vow and one as a gift offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּמַיְיתֵי שְׁתֵּי עוֹלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 27 by treating the case from step 26 as a possible limit on the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting up a הוה אמינא that the או will reject; the answer is completed in step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separate נסכים are needed only when the two offerings differ, such as in the kind of promise.

steps.title: Even two offerings that are exactly alike need separate libations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer for the או in 'לפלא נדר או שלמים'. Two עולות that are both a נדר, or both a נדבה, might seem to share one set of נסכים. The או teaches that they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where a person brings two עולות both as a נדר, or two עולות both as a נדבה, or two שלמים both as a נדר, or two שלמים both as a נדבה, I might have said: they have one name (עולה) and one kind of promise (נדר), so one set of נסכים should be enough for both. The או teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the answer it started in step 28. It describes the case where we would most expect one set of נסכים to be enough, and says the או rules that out too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28 we thought separate נסכים are needed only when the two offerings differ in something, such as one being a נדר and one a נדבה. Here the two offerings are identical in both type and kind of promise, so sharing נסכים seems even more reasonable. The או teaches that even identical offerings each need their own נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow: 'I take upon myself to bring a קרבן.' If the animal is lost, the person must bring another.
A gift offering: 'This animal is a קרבן.' Only that specific animal is promised.
The flour, oil and wine brought together with certain קרבנות.
'It is one name of עולה': both offerings are the same type.
'It teaches us': the word in the פסוק comes to tell us something new.

phrases.english: But where one brings
two burnt offerings as a vow,
or two burnt offerings as a gift offering,
or alternatively, two peace offerings as a vow
or two peace offerings as a gift offering,
it is one name of 'burnt offering'
phrases.notes: He means both animals are the same kind of קרבן, so nothing sets them apart.

phrases.english: and it is one name of 'vow',
so it should be enough for him to bring libations for one,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אבל היכא דקא מייתי שתי עולות בנדר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the הוה אמינא begun in step 28 and gives the conclusion of the derivation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the need for an extra word by showing the mistake it prevents (צריכותא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two offerings of the same type and the same kind of promise could share one set of נסכים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The או in 'לפלא נדר או שלמים' teaches that even identical offerings each need their own נסכים.

steps.title: What does רבי יאשיה learn from the או in 'of the herd or of the flock'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי יאשיה, why does the פסוק need the word או in 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יאשיה, why do I need this phrase 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another או in the same section and asks what it teaches according to רבי יאשיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן uses this או to teach that one animal is enough for an עולה. רבי יאשיה does use the phrase, but for a different lesson, and he learns the one-animal rule from the separate פסוקים (step 3). So the word או itself still needs a job in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need it?': a question asking what an extra word comes to teach.
'From the cattle or from the sheep': words in the פסוק about נסכים.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoshiya,
this phrase 'of the herd or of the flock',
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:3

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי יאשיה, האי מן הבקר או מן הצאן למה לי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained the או words used for separate נסכים, the גמרא goes back to the phrase 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן' from the start of the amud, which רבי יונתן used for one animal, and asks what its או teaches רבי יאשיה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the או in 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן' teaches according to רבי יאשיה.

steps.title: Even two animals of the same kind need separate libations
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought separate נסכים are needed only for two different kinds of animals, like one from the herd and one from the flock. The או teaches that two animals of the same kind also each need their own נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: this rule applies only to two kinds of animals, but if both are one kind, one set of נסכים is enough for both. The או teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the או blocks a mistake about the kind of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cow and a sheep are clearly different, so separate נסכים would make sense for them. Two sheep, though, might seem to share one set. The או between 'herd' and 'flock' teaches that each animal counts on its own, even when they are the same kind.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It might enter your mind to say': this introduces the wrong idea that the פסוק blocks.
'These words apply...': this limits a rule to a certain case.
Two kinds, here a cow and a sheep.
One kind, such as two sheep.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
this applies only to two kinds of animals,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets, from here to 'הני מילי' in the next answer, belong to the corrected wording. Some versions leave them out.

phrases.english: but with one kind of animal,
libations for one should be enough for him,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: סלקא דעתך אמינא הני מילי בתרי מיני
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows the mistake the word prevents.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two animals of the same kind could share one set of נסכים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each animal needs its own נסכים, even when both are the same kind.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק need 'so you shall do for each one'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק needs the words 'ככה תעשו לאחד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'So you shall do for each one': why do I need this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to one more phrase in the section and asks what it adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'for each one' seem to repeat what the different או words already taught, that every animal gets its own נסכים. So the גמרא asks what new case they cover.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So' or 'in this way'.
'You shall do'.
'For each one': for every single animal.

phrases.english: 'So you shall do for each one,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:12

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the או words, the גמרא asks about a further phrase that seems to repeat the same lesson.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'ככה תעשו לאחד' adds beyond the או words.

steps.title: Even offerings set aside at the same moment need separate libations
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought separate נסכים are needed only when the offerings were set aside one after the other. The פסוק teaches that even offerings set aside at the same time each need their own נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: this rule applies only when the offerings were set aside one after the other, but if they were set aside at the same time, one set of נסכים is enough. The פסוק teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'ככה תעשו לאחד' blocks a mistake about timing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two animals were set aside one after the other, each clearly stands on its own. If they were set aside together in one moment, they might seem to form one unit with one set of נסכים. The פסוק says 'for each one', so every animal gets its own נסכים in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One after the other': the offerings were set aside at separate times.
'At the same time': both were set aside together in one moment.
'It would be enough for him'.

steps.whatToRemember: Every animal needs its own נסכים, with no exceptions. Each extra word in the פסוק closes off a different reason to think they could share: a נדר and a נדבה brought together, offerings that differ only in type, offerings that differ only in the kind of promise, offerings that are exactly alike, two animals of the same kind, or animals set aside at the same time.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
this applies only when they were set aside one after the other,
phrases.notes: The closing square bracket ends the corrected wording that began in the last answer.

phrases.english: but if they were set aside at the same time,
libations for one should be enough for him;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: סלקא דעתך אמינא הני מילי בזה אחר זה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows the mistake the phrase prevents.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Offerings set aside at the same time could share one set of נסכים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even offerings set aside together each need their own נסכים.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the מצורע's חטאת and אשם need נסכים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the exception in the משנה and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that the חטאת and אשם of a מצורע do need נסכים. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the exception in the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As a general rule, a חטאת and an אשם do not get נסכים. The מצורע is a special exception to that rule. Since it breaks the pattern, the גמרא wants a clear source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת who brings offerings as part of becoming pure
Sin offering
Guilt offering
The flour-and-oil מנחה and the wine that go along with certain animal offerings
From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: Except that the sin offering of a metzora
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. It said that a חטאת and an אשם usually don't need נסכים, and the מצורע is the exception.

phrases.english: and his guilt offering require libations;
from where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the דרשות about separate נסכים (steps 29-33) to the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוקים for the rule that the מצורע's חטאת and אשם need נסכים.

steps.title: The three tenths of flour are a מנחה that comes with animal offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'three tenths of flour' in the פסוקים of the מצורע as a מנחה that accompanies animal offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: the פסוק 'and three tenths of fine flour for a מנחה' is talking about a מנחה that comes together with an animal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says the flour in the מצורע's פסוק is the flour of נסכים, not a separate מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצורע brings three lambs: an עולה, a חטאת and an אשם. If the three tenths of flour are a מנחה that goes with the animals, then each of the three animals has its own tenth as מנחת נסכים. That is the first sign that his חטאת and אשם also get נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, a measure of flour
Fine flour
A flour offering that comes along with an animal offering, as part of its נסכים

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"And three-tenths of fine flour for a meal offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:10. The מצורע brings three lambs, so there is a tenth of flour for each one.

phrases.english: it is about a meal offering that comes with an animal offering
that the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מצורע's three tenths of flour are a מנחה of נסכים, one for each of his animal offerings.

steps.title: Maybe it is a מנחה that comes by itself?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether this flour might be its own separate מנחה rather than נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it is a מנחה that comes with an animal. But maybe it is a מנחה that comes all by itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading. Maybe the flour is a separate flour offering and has nothing to do with the animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the flour were its own מנחה, it would prove nothing about נסכים for the חטאת and אשם. So the ברייתא has to rule out this other reading.

keyTerms.meaning: By itself, independent
'You say this... or maybe it is only that': a ברייתא formula that raises another possible reading

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּמִנְחָה הַבָּאָה עִם הַזֶּבַח,
phrases.english: Do you say it is about a meal offering that comes with an animal offering,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּמִנְחָה הַבָּאָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is only about a meal offering that comes by itself?

steps.triggerLanguage: אתה אומר במנחה הבאה עם הזבח או אינו אלא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the flour a מנחה of נסכים, or a separate flour offering?

steps.title: The פסוק puts the מנחה together with the עולה
steps.stepSummary: A later פסוק says the כהן offers 'the עולה and the מנחה' together, which shows the מנחה goes with an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק says 'and the כהן shall offer the עולה and the מנחה', you must say the flour is a מנחה that comes with an animal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question by pointing to a later פסוק. That פסוק joins the מנחה to the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחה is mentioned right next to the animal and is offered together with it. That shows it belongs to the animal as נסכים. So the first reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: You must therefore say
And he shall offer up (on the מזבח)

phrases.english: When the verse says
"And the priest shall offer up the burnt offering and the meal offering,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:20

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר בְּמִנְחָה הַבָּאָה עִם הַזֶּבַח
phrases.english: you must say it is about a meal offering that comes with an animal offering
that the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links the מנחה to the עולה, so it is a מנחה that comes with an animal.

steps.title: But is wine also needed?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the flour alone does not yet tell us whether wine is also required.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I still do not know whether wine is needed too, or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא admits a gap in its proof. The flour has been shown, but the wine part of the נסכים has not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים of the מצורע mention flour but say nothing about wine. Full נסכים include wine as well. So the ברייתא needs another source to show the wine is also required.

keyTerms.meaning: But I still do not know

phrases.english: But still I do not know
whether it requires wine libations or not;

steps.triggerLanguage: ועדיין איני יודע אם טעונה נסכים ואם לאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the proof of the flour and asks about the wine.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the מצורע's offerings also need wine?

steps.title: עולה, זבח and או לזבח cover all three of the מצורע's offerings
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about wine in במדבר is read so that each part refers to one of the מצורע's offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'wine for the libation, a quarter of a הין, you shall prepare with the עולה or for the זבח, for the one lamb.' 'עולה' is the מצורע's עולה, 'זבח' is his חטאת, and 'או לזבח' is his אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings the פסוק about wine for a lamb. It reads each part of that פסוק as one of the מצורע's three offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since each lamb gets wine, and the פסוק is read as including the מצורע's חטאת and אשם, they get wine too. The word 'זבח' adds the חטאת. The extra word 'או' adds the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches us
A quarter of a הין, the amount of wine for a lamb
An animal sacrifice
Burnt offering
A lamb

steps.whatToRemember: The מצורע's עולה, חטאת and אשם all need full נסכים. The flour comes from 'three tenths', and the wine comes from עולה, זבח and או לזבח.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And wine for the libation, a quarter of a hin,
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:5

phrases.english: you shall prepare with the burnt offering or for the sacrifice,
for the one lamb."
"Burnt offering": this is the burnt offering of a metzora.
"Sacrifice": this is the sin offering of a metzora.
"Or for the sacrifice": this is the guilt offering of a metzora.
phrases.notes: The extra word 'או' is what brings in the אשם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about wine from step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in במדבר is read so that עולה, זבח and או לזבח mean the מצורע's עולה, חטאת and אשם, so all three get wine.

steps.title: Why not learn both the חטאת and the אשם from 'זבח'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the word 'זבח' alone could include both the חטאת and the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the ברייתא learn both of them, the חטאת and the אשם, from the word 'זבח'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the ברייתא split up the פסוק. This sets up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זבח' is a general word for a sacrifice, so it could cover both the חטאת and the אשם. If so, there is no need to use 'או' for the אשם. The challenge is about why 'או' was needed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him derive it (from somewhere else)
Both of them

phrases.english: But let him derive
both of them from "sacrifice,"
phrases.notes: 'Both' means the חטאת and the אשם. Then the word 'או' would not be needed for the אשם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 39 divided the words of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'או לזבח' to include the אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general word 'זבח' is enough to include both the חטאת and the אשם, so the 'או' seems unnecessary for this.
